prompt: Name one of the seven deadly sins.
label: Easy Opener
source: Gregory the Great's sixth-century list, as refined by Thomas Aquinas in the Summa Theologiae.
valueLogic: Pride, greed and lust come instantly. Wrath and gluttony follow. Envy sits between, because people confuse it with greed. Sloth is the genuine tail - it is the one most often missed and the one whose original meaning is furthest from its modern sense.
note: Vanity takes pride and rage takes wrath: common-language equivalents. Jealousy is deliberately a non-busting distractor rather than an alias for envy; the note explains the difference.

answers.name: Pride
answers.fact: Traditionally the root of the other six, and the sin that cast Lucifer down.

answers.name: Greed
answers.fact: Avarice in the older lists, from the Latin avaritia.

answers.name: Wrath
answers.fact: Anger. Aquinas held that anger at a real injustice could be righteous rather than sinful.

answers.name: Gluttony
answers.fact: Overindulgence, and in Aquinas it covers drinking and fussiness as much as quantity.

answers.name: Envy
answers.fact: Distinct from greed: envy wants what another has, greed simply wants more.

answers.name: Sloth
answers.fact: Acedia, which originally meant spiritual indifference rather than laziness.

distractors.name: Jealousy
distractors.note: Close to envy, but not the traditional name. Envy wants what you have; jealousy fears losing what it has.

distractors.name: Despair
distractors.note: A sin in some traditions, but not one of these seven.

distractors.name: Chastity
distractors.note: One of the seven heavenly virtues - the opposite of a sin.
